system_architecture.description: Implantable MR flow sensor that quantifies CSF flow rate in shunt catheter using phase-contrast MRI principles. Miniaturized magnet + RF coil integrated into catheter or external patch.

subsystems.name: Miniaturized permanent magnet (B0 source)
subsystems.function: Provides static magnetic field B0 for nuclear spin polarization
subsystems.evidence_source: R332 + external miniaturized NMR literature (Nature s41598-019-47634-2)

subsystems.name: RF coil (transmit/receive)
subsystems.function: Excites spins at Larmor frequency; receives echo signal

subsystems.name: Gradient coil (bipolar)
subsystems.function: Applies bipolar gradient for phase-contrast velocity encoding

subsystems.name: Signal processing (phase extraction + flow calc)
subsystems.function: Extracts phase shift; computes velocity from phase difference

key_equations: dphi = gamma * M1 * v                 [phase-contrast MRI velocity encoding]
mr_model.larmor_frequency: omega = gamma * B0; for proton at 1 T, f = 42.58 MHz
mr_model.phase_contrast_principle: Bipolar gradient encodes velocity as phase shift: dphi = gamma * M1 * v, where M1 is first gradient moment and v is velocity
mr_model.snr_scaling: SNR proportional to B0 (higher field = more polarization); also proportional to sqrt(N) (averaging); voxel volume affects SNR
mr_model.critical_parameter: B0 field strength, gradient amplitude, coil sensitivity, voxel size
mr_model.miniaturization_challenge: Standard MRI uses 1.5-3 T magnets (room-size); miniaturized NMR uses 0.1-1 T permanent magnets (palm-size); catheter-scale is unprecedented

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: Protons in flowing CSF experience phase shift under bipolar gradient; static protons have zero net phase; flowing protons have phase proportional to velocity
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Phase-contrast MRI: stationary tissue has zero phase accumulation under bipolar gradient; moving spins accumulate phase dphi = gamma * M1 * v. Two acquisitions (bipolar polarities) yield phase difference proportional to velocity.

flow_measurement_model.model: dphi_measured = gamma * M1 * v; v = dphi / (gamma * M1); Q = v * A_cross_section
flow_measurement_model.velocity_encoding_target: VENC = pi / (gamma * M1) — gradient moment chosen for expected velocity range
flow_measurement_model.status: MODELLED — no hardware validation at catheter scale

governing_model.summary: Phase-contrast MRI flow measurement: bipolar gradient encodes velocity as phase shift; two acquisitions with opposite gradient polarities yield phase difference proportional to velocity.
equations: omega = gamma * B0   [Larmor frequency for P-29 miniaturized magnet at catheter scale]
dphi = gamma * M1 * v   [phase encoding of CSF flow velocity in P-29 catheter-scale MR sensor]
Q = v * A   [volumetric flow from velocity]
SNR ~ B0 * sqrt(N * voxel_volume) / sqrt(BW)   [SNR scaling]
assumptions: CSF protons behave as in bulk water (valid approximation)
B0 field stable over measurement period
RF coil sensitivity uniform over measurement volume
Motion artifacts (patient motion, physiologic motion) separable from flow
boundary_conditions: B0: 0.1-1 T typical for miniaturized permanent magnets (vs 1.5-3 T clinical MRI)
Flow velocity: 0.1-10 cm/s typical in shunt catheter
Measurement volume: catheter lumen (~1-2 mm diameter, ~1-5 cm length)
parameter_sensitivities: B0 — SNR scales linearly; higher B0 = better SNR but harder to miniaturize
M1 (gradient first moment) — determines VENC and velocity sensitivity
Coil sensitivity — affects SNR; miniaturized coils have lower sensitivity
Voxel volume — larger voxel = better SNR but lower spatial resolution
N (averaging) — sqrt(N) improvement in SNR at cost of acquisition time
failure_regimes: B0 too low -> SNR insufficient for phase measurement
Gradient coil too weak -> VENC too high for slow CSF flow
RF coil sensitivity too low -> SNR insufficient

engineering_core.external_precedent: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT ≠ INVENTION_VALIDATION — published miniaturized NMR literature (Nature s41598-019-47634-2) establishes that portable NMR is feasible at low field. Published phase-contrast MRI literature establishes that flow quantification is feasible in clinical MRI. They do NOT establish that the proposed catheter-scale MR flow sensor achieves clinically useful SNR or accuracy.
